courses.title: Introduction to Arthropods
courses.description: Arthropods and certain relatives affecting food, plants, animals, people, and their structures. Emphasizing insects, mites, ticks, spiders, and miscellaneous related groups; their morphological and phylogenetic relationships; habits and habitats; important characteristics affecting the well-being of people. Corequisite(s): PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Introduction to Arthropods Laboratory
courses.description: Arthropods and certain relatives affecting food, plants, animals, people, and their structures. Emphasizing insects, mites, ticks, spiders, and miscellaneous related groups; their morphological and phylogenetic relationships; habits and habitats; important characteristics affecting the well-being of people. Corequisite(s): PLT 2330 .

courses.title: Pesticide Laws and Regulations
courses.description: Federal and California Laws and Regulations affecting individuals, corporations, and agencies providing for the public health, safety and welfare; and protecting the environment including our natural resources. Emphasis on hazardous materials, ground water protection, pesticides, and pest control laws and regulation. Pesticide safety included. Function and structure of pertinent federal, state and county agencies and their enforcement practices as they relate to agribusiness, public health and pest control operations, including case studies.

courses.title: Plant Pathology
courses.description: Basic introduction to Plant Pathology, the organisms that cause plant disease and the conditions that provide the proper environment for disease to occur. Biotic and abiotic disease will be covered. Corequisite(s): PLT 4190L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201 or BIO 2050 ; and BOT 201L or BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Pathology Laboratory
courses.description: Plant pathology lab and field methodologies for isolation and diagnosis of plant disease. Corequisite(s): PLT 4190 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201 or BIO 2050 ; and BOT 201L or BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Integrated Pest Management
courses.description: Concepts of pest management in agriculture, industrial, urban and structural situations. Pesticide categorization, toxicology, safety and formulation. Mechanical, physical, cultural and biological control in pest management systems.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Food Safety and Current Issues
courses.description: [GE 5D] Overview of physical, chemical and microbiological hazards and their role in foodborne illness and the safety of the food supply. Introduction to the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point System. The role of government and basic aspects of food safety laws and regulations. Review of current issues in food safety, food protection, food production, and food processing as they relate to public health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students Laboratory
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Insects and Civilization
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of insects and related arthropods and their influence on life, ranging from everyday events to how they have changed the history of the world. Selected topics on the importance of arthropods in modern and ancient cultures. Course synthesizes biological and historical topics related to arthropods in context of major world events and cultures both past and present, fields of study including science and technology, medicine, world hunger relief, and others. Open to all majors. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Agricultural Insect Pests
courses.description: Recognition and distribution of important insects and mites attacking agricultural crops such as the major field, cereal and truck crops, and citrus, avocado, deciduous fruit, small fruit, berries, grapes, and nut trees. Host preference and identification of damage to plant parts, seasonal history, habits and problems relating to pest management programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 3200L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Agricultural Insect Pests Laboratory
courses.description: Recognition and distribution of important insects and mites attacking agricultural crops such as the major field, cereal and truck crops, and citrus, avocado, deciduous fruit, small fruit, berries, grapes, and nut trees. Host preference and identification of damage to plant parts, seasonal history, habits and problems relating to pest management programs. Corequisite(s): PLT 3200 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 233 or PLT 2330 ; and PLT 233L or PLT 2330L .

courses.title: Weed Science
courses.description: Recognition and control of weeds occurring in crop and range lands, ornamental plantings, and non-cropped situations. Classification of weeds. Cultural, chemical, and biological control practices. Laws and regulations. Corequisite(s): PLT 3310L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Weed Science Laboratory
courses.description: Recognition and control of weeds occuring in crop and rangelands, ornamental plantings, and non-cropped situations. Classification of weeds. Cultural, chemical and biological control practices. Laws and regulations. Corequisite(s): PLT 3310 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 115L or BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Bee Science
courses.description: Care, management, and manipulation of bees. Practical application of principles for effective establishment and maintenance of apiaries. Pollination and value of bees to agriculture. Recognition and control of bee diseases. Recognition and importance of native, commercial and introduced plants as nectar and pollen sources. Corequisite(s): PLT 3360L .

courses.title: Bee Science Laboratory
courses.description: Care, management, and manipulation of bees. Practical application of principles for effective establishment and maintenance of apiaries. Pollination and value of bees to agriculture. Recognition and control of bee diseases. Recognition and importance of native, commercial and introduced plants as nectar and pollen sources. Corequisite(s): PLT 3360 .

courses.title: Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Survey and analyses of the effects of civilization on the environment. Emphasis will be placed on the effects of agriculture and other forms of commerce on food, water, air, soil, and human health.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Ecotoxicology
courses.description: How to think critically about pollutants in the environment - how they interact with biological systems, and how they affect individuals, populations, communities, ecosystems, and our society. Promoting an understanding of: the scientific process for investigating the effects of toxicants on biological systems; the major types and sources of contamination, including environmental disasters; how biological systems and society are affected by, and respond to the issues that pollutants create.

courses.title: Advanced Beekeeping
courses.description: Building upon a foundational understanding of beekeeping and to deepen knowledge and skills in apiculture, advanced topics such as hive management, pest and disease control, bee breeding, and the ecological impact of beekeeping practices are covered. Manage a sustainable apiary, contribute to research, and promote bee health and conservation. Corequisite(s): PLT 4500L .

courses.title: Advanced Beekeeping Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on laboratory component complements PLT 4500. Practical experience in modern beekeeping techniques. Engage in activities such as hive inspections, disease diagnosis, and colony management strategies. Emphasis is placed on sustainable practices, honey extraction, and the use of innovative tools. Learn to assess bee behavior and environmental factors affecting hive health. Corequisite(s): PLT 4500 .

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming
courses.description: The diverse components of agricultural production on a small scale. Examine a number of existing small scale production models. Critically analyze small-scale production systems to determine how well they achieve economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965L .

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming Laboratory
courses.description: Engage in practical activities covering soil health, composting, crop planning, and integrated pest management. Emphasizing sustainable techniques in small-scale farming, the course fosters teamwork and critical problem-solving skills, preparing students to apply sustainable practices in real-world settings. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965 .
